subject: Mathematics

source.title: National curriculum in England: mathematics programmes of study

rules.ks1Ks2Progression: Schools are required to teach the relevant programme by the end of the key stage and have flexibility over when content is introduced within the key stage.
rules.ks3Progression: Progression should be based on pupils' security of understanding and readiness rather than a fabricated year-by-year statutory sequence.
rules.ks4HigherAttainers: Additional higher-attaining content is identified in braces in the official programme.

KS3: Ratio, proportion and rates of change
KS4: Ratio, proportion and rates of change

KS1.summary: Develop fluency with whole numbers, counting, place value, the four operations and simple fractions; apply number knowledge to practical problems.
Use measures to compare and describe length, mass, capacity, time and money, including practical problem solving.
Recognise, describe, compare and classify common 2-D and 3-D shapes and use positional and directional language.
Interpret and construct simple representations of data and ask and answer questions about what the data shows.

KS2.summary: Extend place value and calculation fluency to larger whole numbers, negative numbers, fractions, decimals and percentages, including efficient written and mental methods.
Develop understanding of ratio, proportion and scaling through problem solving and connections with fractions, decimals and percentages.
Use simple algebraic notation, sequences, unknowns and relationships to solve problems and generalise patterns.
Use common units and conversions, solve measurement problems and connect measures with number and geometry.
Classify and describe shapes and angles, use coordinates and position, and reason about geometric properties and measures.
Interpret and present data using tables, charts and graphs and solve problems involving averages and data interpretation.

KS3.summary: Develop fluency, reason mathematically, model situations and solve increasingly sophisticated, unfamiliar and non-routine problems using appropriate representations and methods.
Extend understanding of the number system to integers, decimals, fractions, powers and roots; use accurate calculation, notation, factors and multiples.
Use algebraic notation, simplify and manipulate expressions, substitute values, solve equations and inequalities, work with sequences and connect algebraic and graphical representations.

KS3.domain: Ratio, proportion and rates of change
KS3.summary: Use ratio, proportion, scale, percentages and rates to model and solve problems and interpret relationships between quantities.
Reason about properties of shapes, angles, transformations, coordinates, constructions, similarity, congruence, perimeter, area, volume and measures.
Describe and calculate probabilities, use appropriate representations and understand relationships between likely outcomes.
Interpret, analyse and compare distributions and data, select appropriate representations and use summary measures to support conclusions.

KS4.summary: Consolidate mathematical fluency, reasoning, problem solving and interpretation across the KS4 programme, including exact calculation and accuracy.
Work confidently with powers, roots, indices, standard form, exact values, fractions, recurring decimals, ratio problems and limits of accuracy.
Manipulate algebraic expressions, solve equations and inequalities, work with sequences and functions, and use algebraic and graphical methods to solve problems.

KS4.domain: Ratio, proportion and rates of change
KS4.summary: Apply direct and inverse proportion, growth and decay, compound measures, rates and proportional reasoning to mathematical and real-world problems.
Use geometric properties, similarity, congruence, circle theorems, trigonometry, vectors, transformations and measures to reason and solve problems.
Calculate and interpret probabilities using appropriate models, including combined events and other relationships specified by the programme.
Collect, represent, interpret and compare data distributions using appropriate statistical measures, diagrams and reasoning.

statementPolicy: Objectives are concise TEACHR paraphrases of the statutory programme structure, not substitutes for the official source text. The official GOV.UK publication remains authoritative. Example content and non-statutory notes must not be represented as statutory requirements.
